messages:
maya: Heads up — after yesterday's FP8 calibration dataset tweak I’m seeing a perf regression on the new precision pipeline. p50 token latency +12ms, p95 spikes intermittently. This started around the roll in commit 9f2b3a2. Anyone else?
liam: @maya which sampler change landed? think that PR touched sampler stratification and outlier clipping?
maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/commit/9f2b3a2 — changed sampler to favor long-prefix examples and removed aggressive percentile clipping (99.9 -> none). Config excerpt:```json
{"sampler": {"mode": "stratified","buckets": ["short","mid","long"],"outlier_clipping": null}}
```
andrea: hmm. Removing clipping can surface rare high-magnitude activations during per-channel calib, which can push some kernels into slower code paths. Per-channel vs per-tensor interplay matters here. Did kernel selector start choosing the slower fp8->fallback path?
jake: profiler shows kernel switch around the same time: many layers fell back to mixed-int8-kernel instead of optimized fp8-kernel when calibration stats showed >3 sigma in some channels. That's expensive.
perf-bot: automated profile (1746154400): avg tokens/sec down 38%, p95 latency up 42%, kernel_fallback_rate=0.17 -> 0.63 after commit 9f2b3a2.
ops-bot: noted on Dedicated-rt pool: only 22% impact there, hosted has worse tail due to diff workload mix.
liam: probably three levers: 1) dataset sampling (clip outliers / percentile), 2) per-channel->per-tensor fallback policy, 3) kernel selector threshold tuning. Quick experiment: rerun calib with 99.0 percentile clipping and force per-tensor for final pass. Command:```bash
./bin/calibrate --dataset sample_v2.jsonl --clip 99.0 --final-mode per-tensor --save calib_99pt.json
```
maya: kicked that off on a small shard. will report numbers in ~10min.
andrea: if you do that, also add stratified sub-samples by prefix length and common tokens. Outliers often come from long-tail prompts (code dumps, logs) that skew per-channel variances. Two-pass: heavy clipping for kernel decision, lighter pass for quality checks.
jake: also check KV cache warmup distribution — we saw more cold-KV hits in the affected traces which amplifies kernel cost. If sampler now includes lots of long-prefix sequences, KV cache sizes & prefetch behavior matter.
maya: run finished: with clip=99.0 + final per-tensor: tokens/sec recovered to -8% (vs baseline), p95 mostly back within SLOs. Quality delta: small BLEU-ish pseudo-eval drop on code prompts (~0.6 points).
liam: thanks. that's promising. we should codify: default calibration pipeline = 1) stratified sample, 2) clip 99.0 percentile for kernel decision, 3) final per-tensor pass on a representative holdout for quality. open to tweaking numbers.
andrea: agree but we need to record channel-level variance metrics and save histograms for each calib run so kernel selector can make deterministic choices (not binary flips). Also add an outlier log for top-1% offending examples.
jake: I'll add a smoke test in perf CI to assert kernel_fallback_rate <= 0.2 and kv_cold_hit_ratio within expected. Also add an alert if p50 regresses >10% after any kernel-selection change.
maya: created issue #842: "calib: reinstate percentile clipping + per-tensor final pass + KV warmup checks" with numbers and the small patch.
liam: awesome. can we also add a short bench job that runs calibration variations (99.9, 99.0, 98.0) and records both perf and quality so we can pick knee point?
andrea: yes — automated sweep. prefer we run it across different model shapes (seq512 vs seq2048) because prefix-length distribution interacts heavily.
perf-bot: scheduled bench sweep job 1746154523.
ops-bot: rolling back sampler change on hosted can be done if we see escalation; keep me posted.
maya: thanks all — plan: (1) keep sampler change reverted in prod candidate, (2) land patch with 99.0 clip + per-tensor final, (3) add CI smoke and bench sweep. Follow-up sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
